packages.name: Camp Lemonnier
packages.operator: United States; host Djibouti
packages.role_source: SOURCE CLAIM: Djibouti, at the entrance to the Red Sea and the Bab-el-Mandeb, hosts the densest cluster of foreign bases. The US operates Camp Lemonnier, a former French Foreign Legion base with 4,500 personnel and the 'primary operational headquarters for U.S. Africa Command in the region' (R01:49). AFRICOM relies on it as a critical node for counter-terrorism, drone operations and maritime security at the Bab-el-Mandeb (R03:44). Players must navigate the presence of the PLA base 'without triggering unintended escalation' (R01:70). CHECK: AFRICOM's HQ is in Stuttgart, and the Lemonnier command is usually described as CJTF-HOA, so treat it as a regional hub. The personnel figure is time-sensitive and is not an asset count. No drone types are named. R01 and R03 use similar framing, which is not corroboration. SCENARIO CHOICE: a small expeditionary air element, no ships.
packages.position: Public approx 11.55N 43.15E (south side of Djibouti-Ambouli airport). Approx, verify; outside knowledge. In-game evidence: no unit; nearest proven land and sea points 62-68 NM from Djibouti city; 19 missions in mod 3796349767 centred at 13.17,43.15 (about 97 NM anchors); stock sea point [Bab El Mandeb] at 12.618,43.344, about 65 NM away. The snapper has no proof, so use the land mask or a new extract. The French and Japanese facilities are also described publicly as adjoining the airport (outside knowledge), so separate airbase units near one runway need an editor check.

packages.role_source: SOURCE: maritime patrol/ASW, 333 Sqn with five P-8A named Vingtor, Viking, Ulabrand, Hugin, Munin, delivered 2021-22, hunting Kola submarines (R03:115; R01:61). 'Cornerstone of NATO's maritime domain awareness in the High North'; 8 bn NOK upgrade 'to support next-generation aircraft' (R03:115, added per fidelity[1]). F-35A QRA base that took over from Bodo F-16s; intercepts Tu-142/Tu-95 over the Barents 'in international airspace' (R03:117). Staging for US/UK P-8A, as well as RC-135 Rivet Joint (operator not stated); 'ASW kill web'; UK P-8A North Pole flyover, undated (R03:117). NASAMS III air-defence battalion and counter-UAS (R03:117; repeated R03:162 - not corroboration). Kola submarines must first evade Evenes P-8As; data handoff to UK/US aircraft (R03:166). R03:166 simulation guidance, verbatim: 'target data is handed off across allied platforms via data links, requiring the simulation to model shared situational awareness rather than individual unit vision cones' (the SCENARIO departs from it; see checks). P-8A type row: APY-10, Harpoon, Mk 54 (R03:131).
